title: Past Tense 1: Regular Formation
description: The regular past tense in Russian. Drop the -ть of the infinitive and add -л / -ла / -ло / -ли. The form agrees with the SUBJECT in gender and number, not with the speaker.
descriptionRussian: Правильное прошедшее время: убираем -ть инфинитива и добавляем -л / -ла / -ло / -ли. Форма согласуется с подлежащим по роду и числу.
intro: The Russian past tense is simpler than the present in one way and stranger in another. Simpler because there are no person endings at all: I, you and he take the same form. Stranger because the form does change for gender, so a woman and a man saying the same sentence about themselves say it differently. Four endings cover the whole tense.
rules: Past tense regular formation: drop the -ть of the infinitive and add -л (masc sg), -ла (fem sg), -ло (neut sg), or -ли (plural).
The past tense agrees with the SUBJECT in gender (singular) and number, not with the speaker. 'Я читал' uses -л if the speaker is male; 'я читала' uses -ла if the speaker is female.
There are no person endings in the past tense. 'Я читал', 'ты читал', and 'он читал' all use the same form; the pronoun supplies the person.
The neuter -ло is used with neuter noun subjects (письмо лежало) and in impersonal phrases (было холодно). The plural -ли is one form regardless of subject gender.
Быть (to be) follows the same regular recipe: был / была / было / были. Антон был дома; Маша была дома.
examples: Антон читал журнал. (Anton was reading a magazine.) Anton is masc, so the verb takes -л: читал.
Маша читала книгу. (Masha was reading a book.) Маша is fem, so the verb takes -ла: читала.
Письмо лежало на столе. (The letter was lying on the table.) Письмо is neut, so the verb takes -ло: лежало.
Студенты гуляли в парке. (The students were walking in the park.) Plural subject, so the verb takes -ли: гуляли.
Я работал в Москве. (I was working in Moscow; speaker is male.) Speaker is masc, so the verb takes -л: работал.
Я работала в Москве. (I was working in Moscow; speaker is female.) Speaker is fem, so the verb takes -ла: работала.

tables.title: Six Verbs in the Four Slots

items.hint: Anton is one person, masculine. Which slot is that?
items.explanation: Антон is masculine singular, so the past tense takes -л: читал. Subject decides the form; the past tense has no separate person endings.
Маша is feminine singular, so the past tense takes -ла: читала. The same -ла would appear with я if the speaker is female (я читала) or ты with a female listener.

items.promptEnglish: The students were walking in the park.
items.hint: Plural subject. The plural ending is one form across genders.
items.explanation: Студенты is plural, so the past tense takes -ли: гуляли. The plural -ли is the same regardless of the subjects' gender.

items.promptEnglish: The letter was lying on the table.
items.hint: Письмо ends in -о. Which gender slot does that signal?
items.explanation: Письмо is neuter singular, so the past tense takes -ло: лежало. The neuter -ло is the rarest of the four endings in personal speech but turns up regularly with neuter noun subjects (письмо, утро, окно, море).

items.promptEnglish: I was working in Moscow. (I am female.)
items.hint: Speaker is female. Which slot does the past tense use?
items.explanation: The past tense agrees with the subject's gender. If the speaker is female, 'я' takes -ла: работала. If the speaker were male, 'я' would take -л: работал. Russian past tense reveals the speaker's gender every time you use it.

items.hint: Лена is feminine. Apply the feminine ending.
items.explanation: Лена is feminine singular, so the past takes -ла: звонила. Звонить is a regular -ить verb; in the past it follows the standard pattern (drop -ть, add -л / -ла / -ло / -ли).

blanks: Дети _____ в парке. (The children were walking in the park.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Дети is plural, so the past tense takes -ли: гуляли. The plural -ли is the standard ending regardless of the children's gender mix.

errorCorrection.explanation: Антон is masculine singular, so the past of знать takes the masculine -л ending: знал. Знала is the feminine form and would fit only a feminine subject (Маша знала ответ). The Russian past tense agrees with the subject's gender in the singular, not with the speaker.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha was doing her homework all evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: Маша is feminine singular, so the past of делать takes the feminine -ла ending: делала. Делал is the masculine form and would fit only a masculine subject. The four past-tense slots (-л / -ла / -ло / -ли) are picked by the subject, not by the speaker.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We were talking about Moscow yesterday.
errorCorrection.explanation: Мы is plural, so the past of говорить takes the plural -ли ending: говорили. Говорил is the masculine singular form and would need a single masculine speaker. The plural -ли is invariant across gender: мы говорили applies whether the speakers are male, female, or mixed.

minimalPairs.explanation: Маша is feminine, so the past of быть takes -ла: была. Был would be required for a masculine subject (Антон был дома). Lesson 2 is all about быть; today we focus on agreement with the subject.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The children were walking in the park.
minimalPairs.explanation: Дети is plural, so the past tense takes -ли: гуляли. Гулял would only be correct with a masculine singular subject like Anton or Иван.

reviewVocab.definition: past tense (the form for an action that happened before now; agrees with the subject in gender and number)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша читала книгу' слово 'читала' стоит в прошедшем времени, женского рода единственного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: agreement with the subject (the past tense ending matches the subject's gender in the singular and is invariant in the plural)
reviewVocab.example: Видно согласование: Антон читал (мужской), Маша читала (женский), студенты читали (множественное).

reviewVocab.definition: person (1st / 2nd / 3rd; in the past tense, person is signaled by the pronoun, not by the verb form)
reviewVocab.example: Я читал, ты читал, он читал — формы одинаковые, потому что лицо в прошедшем времени не выражено окончанием.
